demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Negative Appraisals.value: I should have protected others and I failed
I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.explanation: Within Negative Appraisals, 'I have no future' is a broad, severe hopelessness appraisal, while 'others can see what happened to me just by looking at me' implies a visible stigma/marked external sign. For a trauma of accidentally causing serious injury to another, the latter is hard to justify clinically unless there is disfigurement or public exposure, neither of which is represented elsewhere.

issues.item: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: For a male delivery driver whose trauma was accidentally causing serious injury to another person, the appraisal that others can visibly see what happened to him by looking at him is hard to reconcile with the trauma type unless there are visible injuries or marked stigma, which are not otherwise represented. The other selected appraisals centre on guilt and responsibility, so this item pulls toward a different formulation theme and is not well aligned with the otherwise coherent guilt-based negative appraisal pattern.

vignette: Raj, a 34-year-old South Asian man and married delivery driver, has been struggling with intense guilt and self-blame since a tragic accident three months ago. On that fateful day, while navigating through heavy traffic during rush hour, Raj lost control of his vehicle and collided with another car. The impact was severe; the other driver sustained serious injuries and was rushed to the hospital in critical condition. Since then, every time Raj reflects on the incident, he is overwhelmed by feelings of failure and remorse. He believes that if he had been more vigilant or more skilled behind the wheel, he could have prevented the accident. This belief-"I should have protected others and I failed"-has become a pervasive and constant presence in his mind. Raj's self-blame has only deepened over time. He often isolates himself from friends and colleagues, preferring to avoid discussions about driving or any topic that might remind him of the event. Even simple tasks like loading packages into the delivery van now feel laden with potential consequences. Each time he gets behind the wheel again, a wave of anxiety floods over him, reinforcing his belief that "I will never forgive myself for not doing more." His wife has noticed the change in Raj's demeanor; he is often withdrawn and preoccupied, spending long hours alone, replaying the events leading up to the accident. He avoids social gatherings with colleagues from work and rarely talks about how he feels. When his wife tries to offer support or comfort, Raj pushes her away, feeling that he does not deserve any form of consolation. Raj's occupation as a delivery driver has become a source of acute distress. The roads he drives on every day are now fraught with triggers-busy intersections where accidents can happen, other vehicles on the road remind him of his failure to protect others. Each time he sees another car, he is flooded with memories and guilt. He often skips deliveries or takes longer routes to avoid certain areas, which has led to criticism from his supervisors and a strain in his relationship with his wife who relies on his income. Despite these mounting difficulties, Raj had been holding himself together with the belief that he would eventually be able to move past this guilt. However, the weight of his self-blame became unbearable when he received news that the injured driver was still struggling to recover. This news intensified his feelings of inadequacy and failure, prompting him to seek help. Raj is most afraid that he will never find a way to forgive himself for what happened. He hopes that through therapy, he might begin to understand and process the guilt that has been overwhelming him. His primary goal now is to find a path forward-a chance at redemption and peace of mind-despite his deep-rooted belief that he failed those around him.
